meta.reviewer: Claude (Opus 5) via Claude Code weekly review
meta.coverage: The 15 names he writes about most, plus TSM, AMKR and JBL, which the desk still holds. Micron moved to wait. Nebius and POET are new here and not yet researched. Tesla came off. Written before NVIDIA reports on 26 August and Sivers on 27 August.
meta.disclaimer: Second-opinion research notes on @aleabitoreddit's ideas. Personal research tool — not investment advice.

focus.headline: Memory repriced. The market sold the news.
focus.dek: Server DRAM up 13–18% next quarter with Samsung asking 20%, MU's 16 LTAs and SNDK's Meta deal lock the demand in — and memory names sold off anyway. SNDK joins the book.

verdicts.view: The single most important disclosure in this book landed on 17 August and he has not mentioned it once. NVIDIA signed residual value guaranties on roughly 4.25GW of leases at the Portsmouth site with aggregate payment obligation capped at $105 billion, filed under Item 2.03 as an off-balance-sheet obligation, with an OpenAI affiliate as the tenant and NVIDIA covering the shortfall on OpenAI insolvency or non-payment. It can add credit support for another 3.8GW at its own discretion. His whole method is that Jensen telegraphs the theme a year early and the market dismisses it, and on CW lasers and CPO he earned that. But the thing being telegraphed here is not a capacity buy — it is NVIDIA underwriting its largest customer's credit to get the capacity built. That is a different risk, and nobody in the feed is pricing it.
verdicts.execution: No action before 26 August, and read the filing before the headline. The exhibit carrying these agreements attaches to the 10-Q for the quarter ended 26 July 2026, filed with tomorrow's print. Read that exhibit and the gross margin line first; revenue third. Every supplier position in this book keys off that read, so do not size anything ahead of it.
verdicts.changesMind: Disclosure that the $105 billion is collateralised, or that OpenAI's reimbursement obligation is secured rather than a bare covenant, would make this ordinary vendor financing and take it off the risk list.

verdicts.view: Downgrade. Nothing in his case broke — the shortage is real, 2027 DRAM is sold out, and the MLCC crowding-out work still looks right. What changed is that the desk finally put a number on the base. Micron's quarterly gross margin ran 56.0%, then 74.4%, then 84.6% across the three quarters to 28 May 2026, on revenue rising from $13.6B to $41.5B. That 84.6% is above the roughly 80% Sandisk is guiding to as a 2030 target, and no memory cycle in the industry's history has held a peak anywhere near it. Meanwhile TrendForce has 3Q26 conventional DRAM at +13-18% and NAND at +10-15% quarter on quarter, explicitly slower than 2Q26 on weaker consumer demand and a higher base. The shortage holds; the second derivative has rolled over. At a $1.03 trillion market capitalisation you are no longer paid to own the shortage — you are paid only if 84.6% is a plateau.
verdicts.execution: Hold the 17 August entry at $971.66, which is 6.3% underwater, and trim the position back to a starter rather than adding. No new money above $850. This is a downgrade of future buying on valuation and margin mathematics, not a call that the cycle has turned.
verdicts.changesMind: 4Q26 contract prices re-accelerating above the 3Q26 range, or a Micron quarter holding gross margin above 84% on higher bit volume rather than price, would say the plateau is real and put accumulate straight back on.

verdicts.view: For the first time this year he moved toward the desk rather than away from it. On 21 August he wrote that it is getting much harder to support the name when they keep dropping $500m and $600m ATMs, and that the share structure is becoming shareholder-unfriendly. He is right, and the filings are worse than the post. Shares went 62.4m to 84.6m in twelve months, up 36%, the new $600m ATM at $129.10 adds 4.65m more, and this is the third raise since April for roughly $1.7bn. First-half operating cash flow was negative $73.8m on $343m of revenue. His own caveat was 'even if they're building up capacity' — but the prospectus commits proceeds to general corporate purposes including debt repayment, working capital and acquisitions. Nothing in the filing earmarks a dollar of it for lasers. The demand is real and revenue is up 86% year on year; the financing is a tax on owning it.
verdicts.execution: Still no entry at $108. His own stated level is $80 and the desk's band of $85-95 stands, sized as a starter. An ATM sells into strength by construction, so every rally into the $120s is supply — let it come to the band rather than chasing it.
verdicts.changesMind: An announced long-term agreement that funds capacity directly, replacing ATM issuance with customer prepayment, would remove the dilution objection and justify paying up.

verdicts.view: Last week's pass was right and this week the arithmetic is on the record. The merger agreement sets the Exchange Ratio as Agility's per-share equity value divided by the trust redemption price, which was $10.17 at 30 June 2026 — not by CCXI's market price. Buying at $14.09 therefore pays about 1.39 times trust, an effective pre-money valuation near $3.5bn rather than the $2.5bn headline he has repeated five times. Underneath that sit 13.8m founder Class B shares against 41.4m public shares, a $15.99m deferred underwriting fee payable only on closing, and a $201m PIPE priced at $10.00 while the open market pays $14.09. No Form S-4 is publicly filed — the registration statement went in confidentially — so there are no audited Agility financials to underwrite. He may still be right about humanoid demand and wrong about this instrument.
verdicts.execution: No position. If the exposure is genuinely wanted, wait for the S-4 to go effective and buy AGLT once redemptions are known, accepting a worse headline price for a knowable balance sheet. The outside date is 18 March 2028, so there is no urgency premium to pay.
verdicts.changesMind: A publicly filed and effective S-4 with audited Agility financials and disclosed redemption levels turns this into an underwritable equity and the desk would re-rate it on the numbers.

verdicts.view: Stance unchanged, but the cushion he never mentions is gone. Alphabet's Q2 operating cash flow was $39.07bn against $44.92bn of capital expenditure, so free cash flow was negative $5.86bn, and full-year capex guidance rose to $195-205bn. First-half capex of $80.6bn already nearly matches all of 2025's $91.4bn. He cites hyperscaler earnings as proof of the bull case for everything upstream — record cloud demand, backlog, expanding margins — and all of that is true. The part he leaves out is that Alphabet is now funding its AI position from the balance sheet rather than from the quarter. For a company with this balance sheet that is a choice, not a warning, and cloud growing 82% justifies it. But the multiple now has to survive a capex cycle Alphabet cannot pause without conceding the race.
verdicts.execution: Continue adding on weakness; $320 remains the next tranche level. Core-sized and held for years. Do not treat a negative free cash flow quarter as a reason to stop — treat it as the reason to stop expecting buybacks to support the price.
verdicts.changesMind: Cloud growth decelerating below 40% while capex guidance rises again would mean the spend is running ahead of the demand, and the stance goes to watch.

verdicts.view: Same shape as Alphabet and the same omission. Q2 operating cash flow was $45.39bn against $54.21bn of capital expenditure, so free cash flow was negative $8.82bn, and negative $26.99bn across the first half. First-half capex of $98.4bn is up 72% year on year, and guidance rose to about $220bn explicitly because memory costs went up. That last detail is the most useful thing in the quarter for this desk: Amazon's cost line is Micron's and Sandisk's revenue line, which is why the memory names and the hyperscalers cannot both be cheap. AWS at $42.2bn and up 36.7% is still the fastest growth since 2021, and Jassy guides that capacity constraints persist into 2027. He wants Alchip rather than Amazon, which is the right read of where the torque is and the wrong read of risk-adjusted return.
verdicts.execution: Add on weakness in thirds, with $250 and $235 as the next two tranche levels. Core-sized. This remains the low-variance way to own the demand side of the map.
verdicts.changesMind: Two consecutive quarters of AWS growth decelerating below 30% while capex stays at this level would mean the spending is not converting, and the stance goes to watch.

verdicts.view: Downgraded last week on price; this week the per-share picture got worse in a way his post did not show. He reported the quarter accurately — $1,006.3m revenue, up 24.5% sequentially and 109.3% year on year, 50.4% non-GAAP gross margin, $3.23 non-GAAP EPS, and a $1.225-1.275bn guide — and every one of those numbers checks out against the release. What he did not carry is that the same release shows a $7.2bn GAAP net loss for the quarter, driven by a $7.8bn non-cash charge on extinguishing convertible notes, and that shares outstanding went 69.9m to 89.7m over twelve months. That is 28% dilution funding the growth he is measuring per share. At roughly 25 times FY2026 revenue and 50 times the annualised forward guide, the business is excellent and the entry is not.
verdicts.execution: Stop adding. The 12 August entry at $820.59 is up 1.2% against SMH and stays open — this is a downgrade of future buying, not a sell. Revisit accumulate on a drawdown into the $700s that does not come with a guide cut.
verdicts.changesMind: An FQ2 guide above $1.45bn would say the run-rate is still being underestimated and would put accumulate back on the table despite the share count.

verdicts.view: His favourite high-beta optical long reports in two days and the desk still cannot find the revenue. Q1 2026 net sales were SEK 61.9m, down 22% year on year, with EBITDA of negative SEK 24.7m, against a market capitalisation near SEK 10.7bn — roughly 43 times annualised sales on a business that shrank. The $799m figure the bull case leans on is an opportunity pipeline, up 77% year to date, not backlog and not revenue. The four supports he names are real relationships — JBL pluggables, POET and O-Net optical engines, Ayar optical I/O, GFS foundry work — but they are demonstrations and partnerships, not qualified volume production at a named customer. Management pushed slipped defence revenue into the second half. The 27 August print is where that promise gets tested.
verdicts.execution: Do nothing before 27 August. The 12 July add-on-dip at SEK 47.28 stays open as the record of that call; do not average it down into the print. If H1's slipped revenue lands and a Win Semi CW capacity date is given, this becomes a numbers story and re-entry is arguable.
verdicts.changesMind: A Q2 report showing the slipped H1 revenue recognised, positive EBITDA, and a dated CW capacity commitment would convert this from a story to a position.

verdicts.view: Held at watch, and this week's work explains why the 80% target is less of a leap than it sounds. Sandisk's FY2026 GAAP gross margin was already 71.5% — $14.47bn of gross profit on $20.25bn of revenue — against 30.1% in FY2025 and 16.1% in FY2024. A 55-point swing in one year is a shortage repricing, not a cost programme, and guiding 80% through 2030 assumes that repricing holds for four more years. TrendForce already has 3Q26 NAND contract prices rising only 10-15% quarter on quarter, noticeably slower than the last one. He is right that the $93bn minimum contracted revenue makes this less cyclical than the tape assumes; the desk's objection is that $93bn of contracted revenue against a $221bn market capitalisation is already 2.4 times paid, and contracted revenue is not profit.
verdicts.execution: The 10 August add-on-dip is already banked at $1,603.59. Keep the 16 July core position and add nothing here. No new money until a contract renewal prices at the model.
verdicts.changesMind: The first New Business Model renewal disclosed at pricing consistent with roughly 80% gross margin would convert the model into evidence and put accumulate straight back on.

verdicts.view: The condition set last week was met, so the desk is adding. MACOM held above $240 through a week in which it fell 15.6% with nothing company-specific behind the move: fiscal Q3 revenue was $342.2m, up 35.8% year on year, GAAP gross margin 58.3%, adjusted operating margin 31.5%, and the fiscal Q4 guide is $415-425m with adjusted gross margin stepping to 60-61% and adjusted EPS of $1.97-2.03. That guide implies roughly $8 of annualised adjusted EPS on 78.9m diluted shares, about 32 times at $257, against Lumentum near 50 times forward for the same demand. He mentions it mostly in passing inside optical list-posts, which is why it scores low on attention and high on evidence — the one name in the book where the filings are stronger than the coverage.
verdicts.execution: Add a second tranche here at $257, taking the position to a full Core weight. The 17 August entry at $316.44 is 18.6% underwater and this is a declared average-down on an unchanged guide, not a rescue. Stop adding below $220.
verdicts.changesMind: Fiscal Q4 landing below the $415m low end, or book-to-bill under 1.0, would say the sequential step was pull-forward rather than demand, and the stance goes to watch.

verdicts.view: The numbers argue for an upgrade and the price does not. Q2 revenue was $11.54bn, up 50% year on year, with gross profit of $6.20bn — a 53.8% gross margin against 39.8% a year earlier. That margin expansion is the data-centre mix shift showing up, and it is the strongest single quarter in this book after Micron's. Against that, AMD is roughly 16 times annualised revenue after a 160% twelve-month run, so the 9% one-month drawdown is noise. One correction to the feed: he grouped AMD with Riot's $9.1bn, 191MW twenty-year lease, but Riot's own disclosure puts AMD at 50MW firmly contracted at Rockdale, 25MW delivered and 25MW due November 2026 and May 2027. The $9.1bn tenant is a different counterparty. AMD's case is accelerator share, not colocation.
verdicts.execution: No new money at $457. Wait for either a quarter that holds gross margin above 54% or a drawdown toward $380. This is a name to buy on a disappointment, not on a guide.
verdicts.changesMind: A third consecutive quarter of gross margin expansion with data-centre revenue growing faster than the group would justify accumulate even at this multiple.

verdicts.view: Upgraded last week and the relative-value case got sharper. Coherent's FY2026 non-GAAP gross margin was 39.4% with a 20.5% operating margin, against Lumentum's 46.0% and 29.8%, and Q4 revenue grew 33.8% year on year against Lumentum's 109.3%. It is plainly the lower-quality business. It is also near 7.7 times FY2026 revenue of $7.12bn against roughly 25 times for Lumentum, which is a three-fold valuation gap for a two-fold quality gap. One caution the desk could not clear: the widely quoted line that Coherent will not sell indium phosphide lasers externally could not be verified against a primary source, so do not build the merchant-supply scarcity case on it. The GAAP-to-non-GAAP operating margin gap of 790 basis points is real and should be held against the multiple.
verdicts.execution: Hold the 21 August entry at $289.67, down 4.9%, and add a second tranche below $260. This is the cheap way to own the optical demand the desk is already paying up for elsewhere.
verdicts.changesMind: Gross margin failing to expand in fiscal Q1 while Lumentum's keeps rising would mean the discount is deserved rather than temporary, and the stance goes to watch.

verdicts.view: Unchanged and still the cleanest chokepoint in the book. His 17 August note on the InP substrate price hike is the operative fact — suppliers saying that even with the money you may not get the material is the definition of a bottleneck with pricing power, and AXT sits upstream of every laser name the desk owns. He also used it this week as one of the two ideas he says played out, which is a fair claim. The desk has not independently researched AXTI this pass; the cap dropped it. Treat this as a carried stance rather than a refreshed one.
verdicts.execution: Hold the 12 August entry at $73.78. No change this week. Queue AXTI first for next week's seat review so the stance is carried on evidence rather than momentum.
verdicts.changesMind: InP substrate pricing rolling over, or a competitor qualifying capacity at a major laser customer, would break the chokepoint case.

verdicts.view: Sticky holdover, unchanged. It sits outside the analyst-attention top fifteen because he rarely writes about it directly, not because anything deteriorated — this is the tiering caveat working as documented. The reason to own it is that every accelerator in this book, NVIDIA and AMD alike, is fabricated there, and advanced packaging remains the binding constraint on the whole map. Not researched this pass.
verdicts.execution: Hold the 10 August entry at $270.30. No change. This is a position sized to be forgotten about, not traded.
verdicts.changesMind: A CoWoS capacity glut, or a major customer qualifying a second foundry for leading-edge accelerators, would end the structural case.

verdicts.view: Sticky holdover on a watch-tier name with four analyst mentions all year, carried because the stance is live rather than because the feed is loud. His August note is the whole case: he added in the $40s after the post-earnings drop, citing the NVIDIA $1.5bn deal and the TSMC ten-year agreement, and framed it as a 2028 name with separate 2027 ramps. That framing is still right and nothing this week touched it. Not researched this pass.
verdicts.execution: Hold. No adds — a 2028 story does not need to be chased in August 2026.
verdicts.changesMind: Advanced packaging capacity arriving faster than accelerator demand would remove the scarcity premium and end the case.

verdicts.view: Sticky holdover, unchanged. His case is the 1.6T LRO transceiver ramp plus ordinary cycle recovery producing blended margin upside, and he lists it second among the larger names he likes. The attraction for this desk is that it is the only way in the book to own the optical ramp through a diversified manufacturer rather than a single-product supplier, which matters in a week when the pure plays de-rated 15-20% together. Not researched this pass.
verdicts.execution: Hold. Add only below $200. The diversification that makes it dull is the reason it is held.
verdicts.changesMind: Transceiver programme share loss at its main hyperscaler customer would remove the reason to own it over the pure plays.

verdicts.view: Initiating coverage at watch. It re-enters the top fifteen on sustained attention and the operating numbers are genuinely striking: Q2 revenue of $582.3m, up 454% year on year and 46% sequentially, at roughly 50% adjusted EBITDA margin in AI Cloud, with $8.04bn of cash and reiterated 2026 guidance of $3.0-3.4bn revenue and $7-9bn exit ARR. He noted, fairly, that he wanted a raise and did not get one. The desk has not researched this name — it was dropped by the pre-review cap — and a neocloud reselling depreciating GPUs against multi-year contracts is exactly the kind of business where the balance sheet matters more than the growth rate. Initiating at watch is a statement about the desk's evidence, not about the company.
verdicts.execution: No position. Queue NBIS for next week's seat review, specifically the depreciation schedule, contract duration versus GPU useful life, and how the buildout is financed.
verdicts.changesMind: A pre-review pass confirming contract-covered depreciation and no near-term refinancing need would move this to accumulate quickly.

verdicts.view: Initiating coverage at watch, and his own post is the reason. On 13 August he wrote that he has zero idea how POET convinced shareholders to permit that much dilution, that it now sits on roughly $830m of cash, and that he took only small positions. That is an unusually candid piece of bearishness from a long-only feed and the desk takes it at face value. The asset is real — the optical interposer sits between Sivers' lasers and the engines that reach hyperscalers, and he upgraded his own read from readiness to production wording earlier in the year. But a company with $830m of cash and no revenue scale is a call option on execution, and it has not been researched by this desk.
verdicts.execution: No position. Queue POET alongside SIVE for next week's seat review — they are the same supply chain and should be underwritten together.
verdicts.changesMind: A dated production order for interposers at a named customer, funded without further dilution, would turn the cash pile from a warning into an advantage.
